First we apply the quotient rule, subtracting exponents in the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{p}^{7}}{{p}^{2}}\cdot {p}^{3} & = \\ {p}^{(7-2)}\cdot {p}^{3} & = \\ {p}^{5}\cdot {p}^{3}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then we apply the product rule, adding exponents in the product:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{p}^{5}\cdot {p}^{3} & = \\ {p}^{(5+3)} & = \\ {p}^{8}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{p}^{7}}{{p}^{2}}\cdot {p}^{3}={p}^{8}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
